title: Line past for -er/-ir: -ía; se vende, ¿cómo se dice?, me queda uno

cards.title: -er / -ir line past: -ía
cards.body: Same ending as 'would', but 'would' adds to the whole verb, while the past drops the ending first: comería (would eat) vs comía (was eating).

examples.en: I'd sell it / I was selling it

cards.title: se vende = for sale
cards.body: 'It sells itself' means it's for sale; you'll see it on houses and cars.

examples.en: for sale / it was for sale / it would be for sale
examples.es: se vende / se vendía / se vendería

examples.en: They would break it / they were breaking it

cards.title: Se va a romper
cards.body: Se completes the sentence, so you're not left wondering 'break what?'.

examples.es: Se va a romper. / Va a romperse.

cards.title: ¿Cómo se dice? = How do you say …?
cards.body: 'How does it say itself?' Decir: dice, dices, dicen, decimos. '¿Cómo dices?' asks how YOU say it personally.

cards.title: The many jobs of se
cards.body: Completing a sentence (se rompe), changing the meaning (quedar → quedarse), or creatively making things impersonal: se habla español = Spanish spoken.

cards.title: me queda uno = I have one left
cards.body: 'It remains to me one.' Uno / una = one, dos = two (duo). Me quedo would mean 'I stay'.

examples.es: Me queda uno. / Me quedan dos.
No me queda. / No me quedan.
No nos quedaba. / No nos quedaban.
